Output mentions duplicate check
Output mentions license check
Output mentions README check
Output mentions security scan

evals.prompt: Review PR 2162 for the extension listing
evals.expected_output: Review of the index extension (jmgirard/quarto-index). All mechanical checks pass, it uses the MIT license, and the category is correct. The review must explain that Quarto's native indexing is PDF-only through raw LaTeX and makeidx, so the extension fills a gap rather than duplicating a built-in feature. Quarto CLI discussion 3849 is the canonical open feature request. The verdict is APPROVE, with the repository's recent creation reported as context rather than a finding.

assertions.description: Verdict is APPROVE
Says what problem the extension solves, not just that it is valid
Identifies that native Quarto indexing is PDF-only
Names the native mechanism rather than asserting a gap vaguely
Finds the canonical upstream discussion
Reports repo age or lack of users as context, not as a blocking finding
Uses textual verdict words the template requires

evals.prompt: Review a listing PR adding an extension whose repository has no LICENSE file, no license detected by GitHub, and no license section in its README.
evals.expected_output: The listing requirements demand an open-source license, so this cannot be APPROVE. Expected REQUEST_CHANGES naming the missing license, and a contributor comment draft asking for one. Must not silently downgrade to a warning and approve.

assertions.description: Verdict is not a bare APPROVE
Asks for changes or investigation
License is named as the reason
Produces a contributor comment draft

evals.prompt: Review a listing PR where the GitHub API returns a rate-limit error partway through the checks.
evals.expected_output: Failed lookups must be reported as UNVERIFIED and the remaining checks completed. A rate-limited call must not be reported as a missing README, a missing license or a deleted repository, and the PR must not be approved on the strength of checks that never ran.

assertions.description: Does not approve on the strength of checks that never ran
Uses an unverified state rather than inferring absence
Does not claim the README or repo is missing
Other checks still reported
Recommends investigation or changes rather than approval

evals.prompt: Review a listing PR adding a Lua filter extension. Every mechanical check passes: it installs, the README has install and usage, the license is MIT, the entry is correctly ordered, and the filter is small and clean. The PR author's GitHub account was created 2 days before the PR and has 55 public repos with 0 followers. The repo was created the day before the PR with three 'Add files via upload' commits. The account's repos created in the 14 days before the PR are near-identical 'camp-checklist' style projects across Go, Swift, Vim, Arduino and JavaScript. The repo description ends with a company name and the author link points to the company's commercial website.
evals.expected_output: The mechanical checks pass, but the account is under 30 days old and shows a burst of templated repos across unrelated ecosystems, so the recommendation is INVESTIGATE (submitter footprint), not APPROVE. The report states the observations as facts. It runs no upstream thread search, drafts no upstream comment, and drafts no PR comment asking for fixes or thanking the submitter. Any note for the contributor, if drafted at all, gives no reason.

assertions.description: Verdict is not APPROVE
Names the submitter footprint as the reason
Reports account age or repo burst as facts
Does not draft the usual thank-you and fix-list comment
Does not use accusatory words in any public draft
Does not draft a comment for an upstream quarto-cli thread

evals.prompt: Review a listing PR adding a substantive Lua filter extension. The PR author's GitHub account was created 12 days before the PR. It has 3 public repos, only one of them related to Quarto, and the other two are unrelated personal projects. The extension repo was created 5 days before the PR, has 0 stars and one author, and the commits were uploaded through the web interface. All mechanical checks pass and the README documents install and usage.
evals.expected_output: A new account alone is not a flag: there is no burst of templated repos across ecosystems. The recommendation stays APPROVE, with the young account and repo reported as context. This is the false-positive guard for the submitter footprint check.

assertions.description: Verdict is APPROVE
Does not raise the submitter footprint flag
Reports the account or repo age as context

evals.prompt: Review a listing PR where gh repo view reports licenseInfo with key 'other' and name 'Other', and the LICENSE file is MIT text with the 'THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED AS IS' warranty paragraph removed. All other checks pass.
evals.expected_output: licenseInfo of 'other' means GitHub did not recognise the text, so it is not a PASS. The reviewer reads the LICENSE file, reports that it is an altered MIT text, marks the license check WARN, and the recommendation is APPROVE with notes or REQUEST_CHANGES, never a clean APPROVE.

assertions.description: License is not reported as a plain PASS
Says the license text was read

notes: scripts/self-test.sh covers deterministic behavior: regex metacharacters in names, repository path prefixes, extension discovery when directory and repository names differ, vendored documentation copies, ordering, and cross-file consistency. These evals cover judgments that require a model.
